title.narrative: Supporting the livelihood through Renewable Energy Transition in Ger district (Solar Minigrid)

description.narrative: Mongolia faces significant challenges due to its reliance on coal, particularly in Ulaanbaatars Ger districts. Extensive coal usagecontributes to severe air pollution, which is responsible for over 7,100 deaths annually and substantial economic losses, amountingto annual loss of 10% of the nations GDP. There is an urgent need for a sustainable and affordable heating alternative that eliminatesthe use of coal while ensuring energy security at comparable or lower costs.UNDPs Solar Mini grids for Clean Heating addresses this challenge through a phased, long-term approach to transition ger-areahouseholds to renewable heating. The project builds on UNDPs 2023-2024 pilot, which deployed solar photovoltaic (PV) systemswith battery storage and electric heaters equipped with ceramic thermal storage for individual households in the Chingeltei District.This pilot demonstrated the technical feasibility of a solar-powered heating configuration tailored to ger-area conditions, using asystem comprising a 3.4 kW solar array, a 5 kW hybrid inverter, a 3.2 kWh electric heater with 20 kWh thermal storage, a 4.8 kWhLiFePO. battery, and a CO2 monitoring device. The pilots success aligns with Mongolias Five-Year Development Plan (2026--2030), which prioritizes clean energy transition and air-quality improvementThis project proposed a testing with mini-grid solution based on an solar PV system paired with battery storage to provide renewablepower for household heating through on-grid solutions. This solution is aimed at improving living conditions for 800 households,supporting the replacement of coal-based heating with electric heaters with thermal storage and smart CO2 tracking meters foremissions reporting. The initiative not only aligns with Mongolias clean energy transition goals but also represents a scalableimpact model for other underserved regions.The Project aims to target to create solar mini grids with a total capacity of 2.5 MW, including electric heater
